A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VLM-Pruner work and contain complete, readable main text and supplementary Sections 6–7. Their equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original image/video benchmark experiments, inference-cost measurements, and ablations in Tables 1–13 and Figure 4.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark experiments, efficiency measurements, and main-text and supplementary ablation results.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same max-min pivot initialization, parallel greedy selection with BSS, and similarity-weighted aggregation. No algorithmic component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same nine image-language and four video-language benchmarks. Task and scenario coverage in Sections 4.1 and 7 is unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain identical comparator membership, including the applicable subsets of FastV, SparseVLM, PDrop, MustDrop, DART, and DivPrune. The efficiency and supplementary ablation comparisons are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Both versions retain the same model configurations, token budgets, resolution/frame settings, metrics, and evaluation procedures. Section 4.2 and all experimental table settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: The qualitative cases in Figure 2, structural ablations in Table 6, and hyperparameter analyses in Figure 4 and supplementary Tables 7–13 are identical. No robustness analysis or case study is added or removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Statistical uncertainty reporting remains unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical tables and plotted findings are unchanged, including supplementary results. For example, Table 1 retains 95.61% average performance for VLM-Pruner with 64 tokens, and Table 3 retains 92.58% at 88.9% pruning.

T1.justification: Equations 1–10, the diversity objective, the submodularity argument in Section 3.2, and the complexity discussion in Section 3.3.4 are unchanged. Equation placement shifts slightly without mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about training-free pruning, balancing redundancy and spatial sparsity, preserving local details, and performance across five VLMs and thirteen benchmarks.

C2.justification: Interpretations of detail preservation and efficiency tradeoffs remain identical. The supplementary qualifications concerning large token batches and inability to prune at layer 0 are also retained unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds an abstract sentence stating that code is available and providing the Casey-bit/VLMPruner repository address, absent in v1. Existing implementation settings, hardware information, and evaluation-package details are unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 43 references and related-work discussion remain. Positioning against importance-driven and redundancy-reduction pruning methods is unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract gains one code-availability sentence, and the arXiv version/date stamp changes. The remaining prose, terminology, headings, and section order are unchanged apart from text reflow.

P2.justification: The added abstract sentence causes small line, column, and equation-placement shifts on PDF pages 1–4. Figures and tables are unchanged; rendered pages 5–13, including the supplementary material, are identical.

improvement.justification: The new code-access statement provides a concrete implementation pointer missing from v1, modestly improving reproducibility documentation. Scientific content and supporting evidence are unchanged. The PDFs establish the added access information but do not verify the repository's contents or usability.
